frames.narration: A developer pushes commit a1b2c3 to a branch with an open pull request. The code host sends a webhook. The receiver checks the signature, sees that delivery d-7041 is new, and answers with a success code at once.

The planner reads the pipeline file from commit a1b2c3 and builds a graph of 7 jobs: lint, build, four test shards and package. Only lint and build have no needs, so only those are ready. The status reporter shows the pull request a pending check.

The two ready jobs go into the queue for the label linux-4cpu. The scheduler gives the next free runner to the team with the fewest running jobs, so a burst from another team does not push this build back. There is no free runner, so the autoscaler boots two, which takes about 90 seconds.

A fresh runner starts, registers and pulls the build job with a lease that it renews by heartbeat. If the runner dies, the lease expires and the job goes back to the queue. The job runs in a sandbox with no route to the internal network.

The runner computes the cache key from the operating system, the compiler version and the hash of the lockfile: node-linux-9f3a. The key exists, so 410 MB of dependencies come down in seconds instead of being downloaded again.

The branch is trusted, so the broker gives the job a credential for the test database that is valid for 15 minutes and only for this repository. Meanwhile the runner sends its log in numbered chunks, and the developer watches it live in the browser with the secret masked.

The build is done. The runner uploads the compiled output under the hash 77c1 and is destroyed. The planner now has the tests ready. Test history says they take 12 minutes in total, so it splits them into 4 shards of about 3 minutes each, balanced by recorded time.

Four runners fetch the build output and run their shards at the same time. Shard 2 fails the test checkout_timeout. The planner re-runs only that test, and it passes. A test that fails and then passes on the same commit is recorded as flaky, so it will be counted toward quarantine.

All four shards have passed, so the planner starts the package job, and it passes too. The status reporter updates the check on the pull request, replacing the pending one: all 7 jobs green, with one flaky test reported. The build took about 9 minutes from the push.

A stranger opens a pull request from a fork. The same pipeline runs in the same kind of sandbox. When a job asks the broker for a token, it is refused because the code comes from a fork. The job gets a read-only token and cannot write to the shared cache, so there is nothing to steal and nothing to plant.
